answer: Treat the agent economy as a graph: every agent is a vertex, every completed paid transaction an edge. Reputation flows only along settled edges, and a random walk that wanders from audited seed vertices measures how close an agent sits to the honest core. A sybil farm can mint thousands of vertices, but its subgraph is karst terrain: connected on the surface, yet its edges lead only to itself, with almost no paths back to the seed set. Genuine edges cost real work and payment, so the attacker must buy honest history at market price or stay stranded.
